items.title: Deezer lets users hide AI music; Playhead generates signal chains for producers
items.excerpt: Deezer will add a human-only on/off switch before the end of 2026 so users can fully exclude AI-generated tracks from search; it has already excluded 42M+ AI tracks from recommendations. Separately, Playhead turns a text description of a vibe into an editable DSP effects chain without training on artists' audio.

items.title: Deezer to let users block AI-generated music from search results
items.excerpt: Deezer is introducing an on/off toggle that lets users exclude fully AI-generated music from search results; with it on, AI-generated tracks, albums and related artists won't appear. Deezer already keeps detected fully-AI tracks out of algorithmic recommendations and editorial playlists.
items.note: Same story as the Music Ally item; pick one. Fetched via r.jina.ai (MBW is 403 to curl/WebFetch).

items.title: Lalu's Corner: Who Controls the Digital Version of You?
items.excerpt: A column for independent artists on AI voice and likeness control, from Jason Isbell's suit against Suno and the deadmau5 deepfake to the 'I Run' Jorja Smith soundalike, and how UMG, Sony and Warner are taking different routes on licensing, takedowns and opt-in.

items.title: DistroKid is removing songs in response to UMG lawsuit – and some artists aren't happy
items.excerpt: Following UMG's September lawsuit accusing DistroKid of enabling an AI-slop pipeline, the distributor has begun removing songs, and some artists are unhappy about the takedowns.
items.note: recently_covered: DistroKid takedowns (The Verge). New angle = artist backlash / non-AI uploads removed; curator decide.

items.title: Audiotool reveals six winners from its 'Let's Build!' hackathon
items.excerpt: Audiotool's hackathon winners include Pocket Producer, an AI agent for music producers (ideation category), and A&R Assistant, an AI tool that analyses tracks to estimate earning potential, alongside non-AI tools like Score IO and a BBC Maida Vale reverb.

items.title: The Next Music Economy Will Run on Autonomous AI Agents
items.excerpt: An op-ed arguing that autonomous AI agents could fix music's fragmented rights, metadata and royalty systems and pay creators faster, with human oversight.

items.title: Digital Blackface: The Problematic State Of AI Music
items.excerpt: Producer Louis La Roche examines what he calls digital blackface in AI music, naming the people behind one of the biggest AI-artist operations on streaming services.
